panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: MRI of a human patient demonstrating peripheral ring enhancement and central non-enhancement consistent with tunneling abscesses, typical for Listeria rhombencephalitis. B: Sagittal T1 MR image clearly showing a peripheral ring-enhancing lesion in the pons, a characteristic finding in Listeria rhombencephalitis. C: Sagittal T1 MR image showing a ring-enhancing lesion in the lower pons, consistent with Listeria rhombencephalitis. D: Axial T2 MR image showing hyperintensity in the midbrain, indicative of cerebral edema related to the inflammatory/infectious process. E: Axial DWI MR image showing diffusion restriction in microabscesses within the context of the confirmed diagnosis of Listeria rhombencephalitis.
panels.attribution_text: Ranabahu et al. The Characteristic "Tunnel Sign" on MRI as a Diagnostic Marker of Tunneling Abscesses in Listeria Rhombencephalitis in a Patient With Multiple Myeloma: A Case Report.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.103000. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: (A) Coronal T1 MR image with contrast of the patient’s brain. Yellow arrows indicate multiple lesions in the midbrain, pons, and upper cervical spinal cord. These lesions demonstrate peripheral ring enhancement with central non-enhancement, typical of tunneling abscesses. Right side is indicated. (B) Sagittal T1 MR image with contrast. Light blue arrow shows a lesion in the upper pontine tegmentum with peripheral ring enhancement and central non-enhancement. (C) Sagittal T1 MR image with contrast. Red arrow shows a lesion in the lower pontine tegmentum with central low intensity and peripheral ring enhancement. (D) Axial T2 MR image. Green arrow indicates midbrain hyperintensity consistent with edema. (E) Axial diffusion-weighted MR image. Yellow arrow demonstrates diffusion restriction within small ring-enhancing lesions, consistent with microabscesses.
in_text_mentions: MRI of the brain with contrast was performed on December 23, 2023, and demonstrated characteristic findings of brainstem abscesses with the “tunnel sign,” consistent with Listeria rhombencephalitis (Figure 2A-2E).

MRI of the brain demonstrated characteristic tunneling abscesses in the brainstem (Figure 2A-2E). The presence of brainstem tunneling abscesses, along with a dramatic response to IV ampicillin in an elderly, immunocompromised patient, supported the diagnosis of Listeria rhombencephalitis. Neuromelioidosis was excluded by performing a blood melioidosis antibody assessment.
